blocks.text: A variable in programming functions as a storage container within a computer's memory, allowing for the storage of data that can be retrieved and manipulated later in the code. In the example below, the variable age is utilized to hold numerical data. The value of a variable can change throughout the execution of a program, which is why it is referred to as a "variable":

print ( age ="As - Salaam-Alaikum , dear students ! ")
age = 71
print( "Quaid-i-Azam lived for", age, "years")
age =60
print ( "Allama Iqbal lived for", age, "years")

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The first line is printed as print ( age ="As - Salaam-Alaikum , dear students ! "). It does not run: print() has no argument named age (TypeError). The greeting is printed with print("As-Salaam-Alaikum, dear students!").
This example illustrates how the variable "age" is assigned different values to represent the ages of Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal, which are then printed as part of the output.
